lecture_summary: The lecture applies force and torque equations to three representative situations: a plank at the tipping threshold, a ladder limited by static friction, and an Atwood machine with a massive pulley. Its recurring strategy is to draw appropriate free-body diagrams, choose a pivot that eliminates unknown torques, combine translational and rotational equations, apply constraints such as a = αR, solve symbolically, and check the result physically.

videos.title: Static Equilibrium - Tension, Torque, Lever, Beam, & Ladder Problem - Physics
videos.reason: The strongest compact match for the first two examples: it covers force and torque equilibrium, useful pivot choices, beams and levers, and a ladder involving friction.

videos.title: Rotational Dynamics - Basic Introduction
videos.reason: Directly matches the massive-pulley portion through rotating pulleys and Atwood machines, connecting Newton’s laws for the masses with rotational dynamics for the pulley.

coverage_gaps: No playlist entry explicitly describes the lecture’s two-support tipping condition: the departing support force becomes zero and torque is balanced about the remaining support. The beam-and-lever material in the first selection is closely related, but this exact threshold method is not advertised.
